title: Break The Spin · Nov 19
subtitle: 4 posts from Scott source images, all real photos.

posts.theme: The viral "75% want Trump imprisoned" poll does not exist
posts.quote: THAT VIRAL "POLL" SAYING 75% OF AMERICANS WANT TRUMP IMPEACHED AND IMPRISONED? IT DOESN'T EXIST.
posts.alt: Official portrait photo of President Donald Trump. Bold text below reads: That viral "poll" saying 75% of Americans want Trump impeached and imprisoned? It doesn't exist.
posts.caption:
A graphic claiming "75% of Americans say President Donald Trump should be impeached, tried, and imprisoned" is making the rounds on Facebook again. Some versions credit CNN. Others just say "reports claim."

We went looking for the poll. There isn't one.

The claim first spread on X in September and October, posted by accounts like "QAnonObserver" and "X Global," with the line "CNN reports that 75% of Americans..." Not one of those posts linked to a poll. No question wording, no sample size, no dates, no pollster. The websites that repeated it cited the social media posts themselves, not CNN, and a fact-check of the viral claim rated it false.

A real poll comes with a pollster's name, the exact question, the number of people surveyed and the dates it was taken. This one has none of that, because it was never taken.
posts.first:
Why spread a fake number like this? Because it is designed to make Trump supporters feel outnumbered and make his opponents feel like a conviction is a foregone conclusion. Impeachment is a vote in Congress, not a poll, and imprisonment requires a trial and a jury. A meme can't do either.

This is exactly how misinformation works on social media. Someone invents a big round number, attaches a trusted name like CNN to it, and it gets shared thousands of times before anyone checks.

Before sharing any poll, look for three things: who ran it, what they asked, and where to find it. If a post can't answer those, it isn't a poll.

posts.theme: Sanders wants Medicare at 55, passed with 51 votes
posts.quote: BERNIE WANTS TO DROP THE MEDICARE AGE TO 55 AND PASS IT WITH JUST 51 VOTES. MEDICARE'S HOSPITAL FUND RUNS DRY IN 2033.
posts.alt: Photo of Sen. Bernie Sanders in front of a row of flags. Bold text below reads: Bernie wants to drop the Medicare age to 55 and pass it with just 51 votes. Medicare's hospital fund runs dry in 2033.
posts.caption:
Bernie Sanders already has his first demand for the new Democratic Congress.

"As an immediate first step to Medicare for All, the new Democratic Congress must lower the Medicare eligibility age to 55, cover all kids & expand Medicare for dental, vision & hearing," Sanders posted on X. "All of this can be passed with 51 votes in the Senate through reconciliation."

Reconciliation is the budget process that lets the Senate skip the filibuster. With Democrats controlling both chambers in January, they could in theory pass it without a single Republican vote. Sanders even said he is "not absolutely certain" President Trump would refuse to sign it.

Not every Democrat is on board yet. Rep. Richard Neal, the top Democrat on the House Ways and Means Committee, said he doesn't know about 55 but is "open to a conversation about it."
posts.first:
Here is what the pitch leaves out. Medicare's hospital insurance trust fund is already projected to run dry in 2033, according to this year's Medicare Trustees Report. After that, it could pay only about 89% of scheduled hospital benefits.

When the Congressional Budget Office studied a smaller step, lowering the age to 60, it estimated it would add $155 billion to deficits over six years. Going all the way to 55, and adding dental, vision and hearing coverage on top, would cost far more. Sanders has not put a price tag on it.

"Free" health care is never free. Adding millions of people to a program that is already short on money means higher taxes, bigger deficits or cuts somewhere else. Before Congress expands Medicare, it should prove it can keep the promises it already made to seniors.

posts.theme: White House requires sign-off before staffers testify
posts.quote: THE WHITE HOUSE TO DEMOCRATS PLANNING INVESTIGATIONS: NO FEDERAL STAFFER TESTIFIES WITHOUT OUR SIGN-OFF.
posts.alt: Two panels: a photo of White House Counsel Will Scharf in the Oval Office on the left and an official portrait photo of Rep. Robert Garcia on the right. Bold text below reads: The White House to Democrats planning investigations: no federal staffer testifies without our sign-off.
posts.caption:
Democrats take control of Congress in January with a long list of investigations planned. The White House just drew its line.

White House Counsel Will Scharf sent a one-page memo to every executive branch agency requiring approval from both the White House Counsel's office and the Office of Legislative Affairs before any employee agrees to appear before a congressional committee, Axios first reported.

A White House official said the administration "will not be extorted, intimidated, or threatened into submission" by "politically motivated baseless investigations." The official added, "We are ready to engage with Congress," and "This process ensures reasonable requests are respected."

Scharf had already warned the incoming House Oversight chairman, California Democrat Robert Garcia, that "Congressional investigations must further a legitimate legislative task," and that Congress "cannot employ them to exercise powers of criminal prosecution assigned to the Executive and the Judiciary."
posts.first:
This is not new territory. The Pentagon adopted a similar rule in October 2025, when Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth required approval before staff dealt with Congress. Administrations of both parties have fought congressional subpoenas over executive privilege for decades.

The memo does not spell out how requests will be judged or how quickly, and the first real test comes when the new Congress convenes in January. Expect court fights and contempt threats from the new majority.

But the message is clear. Oversight is part of Congress's job. Turning committees into a prosecution machine against political opponents is not, and the White House is not going to make it easy.

posts.theme: Trump on blue-state natural gas costs
posts.quote: NEW YORKERS PAY 2.5 TIMES WHAT UTAH PAYS FOR NATURAL GAS. TRUMP BLAMES THE BLUE-STATE PIPELINE BLOCKADE.
posts.alt: Photo of President Donald Trump speaking at the Resolute Desk in the Oval Office. Bold text below reads: New Yorkers pay 2.5 times what Utah pays for natural gas. Trump blames the blue-state pipeline blockade.
posts.caption:
President Trump is taking aim at blue-state energy policy.

"Despite the United States having the MOST ABUNDANT Supply, and LOWEST COST Natural Gas in the World, Citizens in Blue States like New York have been paying 3X-7X more for Natural Gas due to the costly Anti-Energy Policies pushed by Blue State Governors and Political leaders," he posted on Truth Social.

His exact multiple runs high. Federal data for July shows New York households paid $30.86 per thousand cubic feet of natural gas, about two and a half times the $12.38 paid in Utah, the cheapest state. But the gap is real, and so is the reason he points to.

New York sits right next to Pennsylvania, one of the biggest gas-producing states in the country, and it blocked the pipelines that would carry that gas in. Gov. Andrew Cuomo's administration used the Clean Water Act to block the Constitution Pipeline in 2016 and the Northeast Supply Enhancement pipeline in 2020.
posts.first:
Alan Armstrong, CEO of Williams, the company behind both projects, put it bluntly: "the states' ability to block pipelines has been pretty chronic, particularly in the New York City market."

The Trump administration is now pushing to revive the Constitution Pipeline, with the Energy Department reportedly putting $42 million toward it. Some New York officials are fighting back, with one calling it an attempt to "trample our state's rights."

Even Gov. Kathy Hochul has started to bend. In February 2025 she approved a project to bring more gas into New York, saying, "I need an all-of-the-above approach that's going to work."

Pipelines are the cheapest, safest way to move natural gas. When a state blocks them, families pay for it every winter on their heating bills.
